verdict.rationale: Bun's own project data stays in open, standard formats: npm-standard package.json, a text-based `bun.lock`, and a standard node_modules layout. It also documents writing a Yarn lockfile alongside `bun.lock`, which gives a direct exit path to another package manager. Missing for 10: documented export to npm/pnpm lockfile formats, explicit migration-away guidance covering all Bun-specific data (e.g. catalogs, trustedDependencies, bunfig), and independent hands-on corroboration of leaving Bun.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: To write a Yarn lockfile _in addition_ to `bun.lock`: bun install --yarn
Bun v1.2 changed the default lockfile format to the text-based `bun.lock`.
strips catalog and workspace protocols from the `package.json`, resolving versions if necessary
